html:
A railway built from 1903 to 1940 across Anatolia, northern Syria and Iraq to Baghdad, with German money and engineers. It was meant to link Berlin by rail to the Persian Gulf.

The Ottoman sultan Abdul Hamid II wanted it to bind his far provinces together and move troops fast. Germany under Wilhelm II wanted trade, influence and perhaps oil. Deutsche Bank led the financing, and the Ottoman state promised a payment for every kilometre built.

Britain, France and Russia saw a German road to India, Persia and the Gulf. The railway became one of the rivalries that soured relations before World War I. During the war the line was still unfinished: the tunnels through the Taurus and Amanus mountains were not done until 1918, so troops and supplies had to be carried round the gaps.

After the war the line was split between Turkey, French Syria and British Iraq. The last link was finished in 1940. Parts of it, together with the Hejaz Railway to Medina, formed the late Ottoman rail network.
sum: A railway built from 1903 to 1940 across Anatolia, northern Syria and Iraq to Baghdad, with German money and engineers. It was meant to link Berlin by rail to the Persian Gulf.
